rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=50, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=314, rationale=iter-12 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-11 hr=0.0, grad_clip OFF gave rmse=0.00635, ssim=0.942 -- no better than clipped; removing the grad-norm damp did not sharpen. Iters 1-11 all hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: plain-UNet N2I regresses to the over-smoothed FBP mean; no edge-preserving structural guard (bilateral sibling range kernel hr~0.21 is what this solver lacks). (3) ONE KNOB: relative to iter-6 best reference (lr=3e-4, n_iter=50, c=16, grad_clip=1.0), seed 42 -> 314. (4) HYPOTHESIS: VARIANCE CHECK -- re-running the best config under a different RNG seed (warm-start init + train permutation) tests whether hr=0 is robust to seed or a one-off. If rmse lands ~0.0062-0.0064 again (hr=0), the ceiling is seed-independent and structural; a large swing would signal seed sensitivity. The breast VAL SPLIT is fixed (staged h5, seed-20260703), so seed only perturbs training RNG, not the val cases. Per the ceiling, expect hr=0 again. (5) BUDGET: identical to iter-6 (n_iter=50 fast); ~12 min << 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-13 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: lr=1e-4 very gentle, n_iter=400 high, pretrain_steps cap, batch_size=2 warm-start, pretrain_epochs=1 minimal warm-start.
